messages:
Maya Chen: Quick thread — I'm drafting a concise customer-facing enablement checklist for BrightBridge focused on caching, batching, streaming + account-health signals. This will be given to SEs during week-2 handoff and included in the customer enablement email. PTAL @Jonah @Elena @Ravi. Goal: reduce latency/cost while minimizing quality regressions.

Jonah Park: SGTM. A couple of quick defaults I recommend we call out up front: cache_ttl_short=60s for conversational prefixes, cache_ttl_long=24h for embeddings, and prefer idempotent prefix caching only for deterministic prompts. Mention token budget checks.

Elena Ruiz: Adding a tiny sample SDK + streaming example that we can paste into the customer doc:

```js
// Node SDK pseudocode - enable prefix cache + stream
const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});
const stream = client.chat.stream({
  model: 'redwood-enc-2',
  cache: { prefix: true, ttl_seconds: 60 },
  batching: { max_batch_size: 8, max_latency_ms: 50 }
});
stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
```

Elena Ruiz: And a curl SSE example for customers who use server-sent events:

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-enc-2
```

Ravi Singh: On batching: start with max_batch_size=8 and max_latency_ms=50 for most web workloads. If customer qps > 200, switch to dynamic batching with adaptive backoff. Also include guidance: if p95 latency > 300ms with batching on, revert to single-call low-latency mode and file a perf ticket.

Maya Chen: Renewal-risk and account-health signals we should capture in the runbook: weekly active seats drop >30%, evaluation failure rate increase >5% (compare eval baseline), consistent billing anomalies (>=3x expected), and >2 open P1 incidents in 30 days. When any trigger hits, escalate to AM + Solutions and schedule a health-check call within 48h.

Lottie Marsh: For enablement coordination — recommend a 15-min checklist call with these agenda items: 1) quick architecture review, 2) cache & batch defaults, 3) streaming demo, 4) telemetry + feedback link. I can own scheduling and the call script.

Maya Chen: For feedback capture: include a short form we can send after week 1 with 3 quick metrics (latency satisfaction, quality thumbs up/down, any regressions). Example link placeholder: https://intra.redwood/feedback/brightbridge. Also add an opt-in prompt-sample library so SEs can repro and test.

Elena Ruiz: Telemetry naming convention suggestion: tags like `cs:onboard:cache`, `cs:onboard:batch`, `cs:onboard:stream` and an eval suite named `brightbridge_onboard_v1`. Add a short JSON example for telemetry events to paste into docs:

```json
{"event":"inference_request","tags":["cs:onboard:cache","brightbridge"],"latency_ms":42}
```

Jonah Park: Small note: call out safe-guard for caching with PII — prefix caching must be disabled if any input contains PII markers. Add sample filter rule in the doc.

Maya Chen: Plan: I'll compile this into a one-page enablement checklist + email template and post to Confluence. Jonah — can you finalize the code snippets? Ravi — please add the perf fallback steps. Lottie — will you own the renewal-monitoring thresholds and scheduling?

Lottie Marsh: :thumbsup: Assigning now. I'll also draft the 15-min script and the week-1 feedback form.

deploy-bot: Published page cs-enablement/brightbridge-v1 to Confluence (draft).

Maya Chen: Awesome — thanks everyone. Once Confluence is updated I'll attach the checklist to the customer record and create the monitoring alerts. If anyone wants to add short FAQs for customers (e.g., why streaming vs polling), drop them here and I'll fold them in.
